doc.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010

title: The six-week Miles tour and then Sonny Rollins and J.J. Johnson
summary: He recalls the Seven Steps to Heaven band forming on the tour, Miles saying he could swing, and joining J.J. Johnson afterward.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: during that time he had been known to maybe do that, “I changed my mind.” Because what he did, like on the “Seven Steps to Heaven” date, that was conceived when I was in the band on that tour. And we had a great time. Jimmy Cobb will tell you about it, Roy talks about it in the book. There was me, so he asked me, “Do you know a good alto player?” I said, “Yeah, Frank Strozier.” He said, “What’s Frank doin’?” Because he knew us from Chicago. So I told Frank to go by but Frank was reluctant. So his wife says, “No Frank, you should go,” because George Coleman was already hired. Because Coltrane recommended George Coleman for the gig. And Ron Carter was going to be in the band, and Jimmy Cobb was just finishing up a tour so Tony Williams was going to join the band. And we had a great six weeks. Miles made every gig. And there were times when he’d tell me if I didn’t play a certain note at a certain chord he was going to strand me, meaning like they would leave and leave me in a city by myself. But I didn’t care, because I always kept me some bus money or some airfare, you know what I mean. He was teasing you know what I mean. But he told me, “You sure can swing.” Well when he said I sure can swing that was a compliment coming behind Wynton Kelly, because there’s nobody swinging harder than Wynton Kelly. So we had a great six weeks. He’d get to the gig at the Shelly’s Manne Hole before time, “Let’s play some music.” You know he was a practical — he was always messing with you. He always supported me, even after I left the band he supported me. He had me on a regular standing, “You’ve really got your stuff together now.” So during that time I was talking to Mulgrew that I didn’t really understand modes. For some reason. I look at it now and I say it’s easy to understand modes, you know [scats] with the voicing. So Mulgrew says, “Hey man, a whole lot of piano players didn’t understand modes at that time. You know it seems so simple now, just the basic idea of how you’re supposed to do it with clusters of stuff. But then, man, it was foreign to me. But so yeah, that was from April 1 until about April 24, man. He said, “I’ve got a gig for you.” So I went and worked with Sonny Rollins at Birdland for a week and then after that I joined J.J. Johnson’s band.
Yeah. As you say, I’ve been around the block a few times.
